Get GTFS errors encountered in network building

Source: R/network_tools.R
get_gtfs_errors.Rd

The errors found in the network's 'GTFS' feeds, as the validator 'gtfs-lib' (Conveyal) reports them. build_network() refuses to build a network when any error has priority "HIGH"; this lists them, also for a directory a network could not be built from.

Usage

get_gtfs_errors(network)

Arguments

network

A network built with build_network(), or the path of a directory with 'GTFS' feeds (.zip), for instance one a network could not be built from.

Value

A table with columns file (the table, without .txt), line (the record, the header being line 1; 0 for a whole table), type (gtfs-lib's error class), field, id (the key concerned, for duplicate keys and suspect stop locations) and priority ("HIGH", "MEDIUM", "LOW" or "UNKNOWN").

Tables are tibbles by default; options(peabiru.output = "data.frame") gives base data.frames and options(peabiru.output = "data.table") gives data.tables (see peabiru-package).

Details

The feeds are read again (the files the network was built from, or the .zip files of the directory given) with gtfs-lib's checks: every check of its table loaders (empty required fields, numbers, times and URLs that do not parse, values out of range, duplicate and missing keys, references to stops, trips, routes, services, agencies and fares that do not exist, tables missing, empty or in a subfolder of the .zip) and of its post-load validation (services, parent stations, stops in places with nearly no population, GTFS-Flex trips), with the file, line, type, field, id and priority gtfs-lib gives. The rows are listed feed by feed, in the order gtfs-lib finds them. A feed on which gtfs-lib fails instead of listing errors (a date that is not YYYYMMDD, a frequency of a trip that does not exist, a service or fare without an id) is an error naming the cause, as is a locations.geojson (of GTFS-Flex zones) that is not in UTF-8. GTFS-Flex zones and location groups are read as gtfs-lib reads them, for its errors; on-demand trips are not routed.

Nothing is written to the data folder. The types of the columns are those data.table::fread() would give a file of these rows: a column with no value at all (often field or id) is logical, line is an integer.

See also

Other network functions: build_network(), check_transit_availability(), find_snap(), street_network_bbox(), street_network_to_sf(), transit_network_to_sf()

Examples

data_path <- system.file("extdata/spo", package = "peabiru")
network <- build_network(data_path, n_threads = 2)
get_gtfs_errors(network)
#> # A tibble: 7 × 6
#>   file      line type              field      id    priority
#>   <chr>    <int> <chr>             <chr>      <chr> <chr>   
#> 1 agency       3 DuplicateKeyError agency_id  1     MEDIUM  
#> 2 calendar     8 DuplicateKeyError service_id USD   MEDIUM  
#> 3 calendar     9 DuplicateKeyError service_id U__   MEDIUM  
#> 4 calendar    10 DuplicateKeyError service_id US_   MEDIUM  
#> 5 calendar    11 DuplicateKeyError service_id _SD   MEDIUM  
#> 6 calendar    12 DuplicateKeyError service_id __D   MEDIUM  
#> 7 calendar    13 DuplicateKeyError service_id _S_   MEDIUM
